name: CapCut Graph Curve Easing Control
use_when: A CapCut keyframed zoom, move, rotation, overlay path, or color/volume change feels linear, robotic, or abrupt.
The editor needs to control how motion starts, accelerates, slows, or stops between keyframes.
A CapCut-style move needs to translate into Remotion, ffmpeg, Premiere, DaVinci, or Blender easing metadata.
A documentary cutout, background, or parallax collage needs professional scale/X/Y motion rather than flat linear movement.
avoid_when: A tested built-in animation already gives the correct motion and timing.
The editor has not named the job of the movement.
The motion needs to feel intentionally mechanical, flat, or jarring.

timeline_pattern.pattern: start_keyframe -> end_keyframe -> open_graph -> shape_start_speed -> shape_end_speed -> preview -> tune_or_reset
timeline_pattern.start_rule: The left side of the graph controls the start of the motion: lower starts feel slower, higher starts feel faster.
timeline_pattern.end_rule: The right side controls the end: lower endings settle gently, higher endings stop more sharply.
timeline_pattern.direction_rule: A curve rising upward accelerates; a curve moving downward decelerates.
timeline_pattern.linear_rule: A middle/straight line keeps speed more constant and can feel mechanical when the move needs polish.
timeline_pattern.smoothness_rule: Smooth curves usually feel natural; very sharp changes should be reserved for intentional impact.
timeline_pattern.reapply_rule: If a keyframe is moved after a Cubic Ease pass, reapply or recheck the curve because the graph can change with the new timing.

motion.rule: Shape the graph to match the emotional job of the move, then verify the subject remains readable.

keyframe_values.slow_start: Use a lower left-side curve when the move should ease into motion.
keyframe_values.fast_start: Use a higher left-side curve when the move should begin immediately.
keyframe_values.gentle_end: Use a lower right-side curve when the final focus should settle cleanly.
keyframe_values.sharp_end: Use a higher right-side curve only for intentional hard stops, impacts, or snap edits.
keyframe_values.constant_speed: Use a flatter middle line only when even speed is the desired style.
keyframe_values.documentary_cubic: For CapCut documentary parallax, apply Cubic Ease to scale, X, and Y after setting the motion path, then recheck each subject target.

sound.rule: Add SFX only when the graph-shaped motion creates a visible hit, snap, or reveal; many eased moves need no sound.

captions.rule: Caption readability must be checked after graph changes because a faster start or sharp stop can move text under the focal point.

color.rule: Graph-shaped color or effect changes should preserve readable faces, proof, products, and captions through the whole curve.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent the graph as easing metadata for scale, crop, x/y, rotation, opacity, color, or volume expressions; render test frames around start, middle, and end.
implementation.remotion: Store curveType or cubicBezier values and pass them into interpolate/easing functions for transform, opacity, color, and volume changes.
implementation.blender: Use the Graph Editor to shape F-curves for transform, material, or audio animation; check interpolation handles rather than leaving default linear motion.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create the property keyframes, open Graphs on the selected keyframe, choose or shape the curve, then preview the actual movement before copying it to more clips. For parallax scenes, apply Cubic Ease to scale, X, and Y, and reapply it after moving keyframes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Effect Controls temporal interpolation, Bezier handles, Ease In/Ease Out, or the Velocity graph to shape start and end speed.

common_mistakes: Confusing keyframe spacing with graph shape and changing only one when the other is causing the problem.
Using a sharp graph because it looks advanced even though the clip needs a clean settle.
Leaving a linear graph on a move that should feel smooth or professional.
Copying a graph preset to every clip without checking different subject motion.
Changing the graph after caption placement and forgetting to recheck collisions.
Moving a parallax keyframe after easing and forgetting to reapply or inspect the Cubic Ease curve.
qc: Can the editor name why the curve should start slow, start fast, settle gently, or stop sharply?
Does the motion avoid unintended linear, robotic, or rough movement?
Does the subject remain readable through the full curve?
Do captions, faces, UI, products, proof, and action remain safe after the graph is applied?
If the graph is copied to multiple clips, was each clip previewed with its own subject motion?
After any keyframe retiming, was the graph rechecked so the documentary move still accelerates and settles cleanly?
